title: The Cream-Ware Invoice That Reported Wedgwood's Amputation
conflicts: Age at amputation: LRB and Spectator say 38, but the ODNB's probable birth date (12 July 1730) makes him 37; no age given. Wedgwood's own 'St Amputation Day' letter points to 31 May, against 28 May on the day's invoice note; 28 May used. One surgeon (ODNB) versus two (Smiles, Meteyard, Swift's note); story names Bent plus a second surgeon. Bentley's presence rests on Smiles and Meteyard's inference, so it is attributed to biographers. Cause: the Spectator says a carriage accident, the ODNB a smallpox-weakened knee plus a 1762 fall and an April 1768 strain; story uses the documented knee history only.
notes: Primary letters are quoted via Meteyard (1866) and Smiles (1897), both on archive.org; the ODNB is cited from a family blog's reproduction because oxforddnb.com is paywalled. The slate's 'Queensware' framing is kept as context (potter to the Queen, Queen's ware); the episode is the amputation and recovery while Etruria was being built.
